manualReview.summary: Twelve selected-gene contexts reproduce numerically; astrocyte cohort match inferred from Methods, nine glial/Ghrh contexts differ by low-count mice
manualReview.note: 2026-11-15 continuation: publisher Supplementary Data 1/4, GEO cell metadata and accepted manuscript re-retrieved with SHA-256 equal to the 2026-09-11 record. The registered DE tables were regenerated after 2026-09-11; recomputation against current tables reproduces the twelve selected measurements (Pearson .9751-.9935, Spearman .9642-.9871, 100% paired direction, selected-author coverage 99.22%-100%). The accepted-manuscript Methods require at least two cells per sample. Under the published Methods rule (>=2 cells per sample) the three astrocyte contexts would select identical mice and deposited nuclei to the registered 20-nucleus rule; the author DE script is unavailable, Arc15 sits exactly at 25 astrocyte nuclei (the pinned PCA helper uses a strict >25 cut), and 75 nuclei are unidentified, so author membership is inferred, not demonstrated. The sub.class grouping cited for the author comes from pinned figure/PCA code, not the DE script; major.class equals sub.class in the deposited metadata for all 5,588 astrocyte, 1,253 OPC and 1,317 oligodendrocyte ARC nuclei. OPC, oligodendrocyte and Ghrh contexts gain 1-3 low-count mice under that rule (for example OPC Arc23 with 5 and Arc30 with 3 nuclei), so their cohorts differ from the registered result. The 75 nuclei separating the paper total 75,787 from the deposited 75,862 are unidentified. All author rows are nominal P<.05 selections, not the tested universe. Sixteen of 28 registered contexts have no matching author coefficient. Evidence: continued-sources/GSE262407/turbo-2026-11-15-partial4/.

comparabilityReview.basis: Current registered Explorer per-track tables, recomputed 2026-11-15; compared only where a named author cell type and publisher-defined contrast exist.
comparabilityReview.reference: Publisher Supplementary Data 1 (ARC/VMH glia) and 4 (neurons): complete named cell-type rows, all nominal PValue<0.05.

cohort.note: Astrocyte contexts: under the published Methods rule (>=2 cells per sample) the author cohort would select identical mice and deposited nuclei; the author DE script is unavailable, Arc15 sits exactly at 25 astrocyte nuclei (the pinned PCA helper uses a strict >25 cut), and 75 nuclei are unidentified, so author membership is inferred, not demonstrated. OPC, oligodendrocyte and Ghrh contexts: the Methods rule admits 1-3 low-count mice excluded by the registered 20/10-nucleus rules. The sub.class grouping comes from pinned figure code, not the DE script; major.class equals sub.class in the deposited metadata for all astrocyte, OPC and oligodendrocyte ARC nuclei.

contrast.note: Publisher descriptions define glucose minus saline within diet and HFD minus control under saline, matching registered case minus baseline. hfd_vs_chow_glucose has no author table.

features.note: Exact symbol join; 0 duplicated author symbols; 6 unmatched selected rows across three non-astrocyte contexts. Methods exclude genes expressed in <=10% of cells; the ^Gm|Rik$ exclusion in pinned Figure_2 voom_wrapper (Fig. 2c PCA) is not applied in the deposited DE tables, which contain Gm/Rik symbols.

effects.note: Both edgeR log2 fold change case minus baseline; Pearson .9751-.9935, Spearman .9642-.9871, 100% direction across the twelve selected contexts.

inference.note: Registered edgeR-QL two-arm fit versus author robust-dispersion glmLRT; FDR calls differ widely and are contextual.

coverage.note: 12 of 28 registered contexts have a selected author reference; selected rows omit the tested nonsignificant tail.

comparabilityReview.criteria: author-concordance-v2 per context within selected scope: >=30 paired genes, >=90% selected-row coverage, Pearson and Spearman >=0.90 or >=90% direction; cohort, contrast, identifier and effect compatibility required. Absent rows are not author negatives.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: Three astrocyte contexts meet every numeric scoped criterion; cohort compatibility is supported by Methods text but not by executed author code. Nine contexts agree numerically but have a documented cohort difference; sixteen contexts unassessed. No dataset-level pass.
